title: Bigger photo, same face?
hook: Enlarge a 4 by 6 photo without stretching the face. What must the long side be?

knows: width and height of a rectangle
doesNotKnow: that a shape is kept by keeping the ratio of its sides, so each side is multiplied by the same number, not increased by the same amount

misconception: To enlarge a 4 by 6 photo without distorting it you add the same amount to each side (6 by 8).
objective: The learner can say that a 4 by 6 photo with short side 6 keeps its shape only at 6 by 9, because both sides are multiplied by 1.5, and that adding the same amount changes the ratio.

claims.text: A 4 by 6 photo enlarged so its short side is 6 keeps its shape only at 6 by 9: 6 ÷ 4 = 1.5 and 6 × 1.5 = 9, and 9 ÷ 6 = 1.5 = 6 ÷ 4.
claims.note: Arithmetic: 6/4 = 1.5, 4 x 1.5 = 6, 6 x 1.5 = 9, 9/6 = 1.5; check A2 re-run.

claims.text: Adding 2 to each side gives 6 by 8, ratio 8 ÷ 6 = 1.33; adding 4 gives 8 by 10, ratio 1.25; neither is 1.5, so the corner leaves the line. Multiplying by 2 gives 8 by 12, ratio 1.5, on the line.
claims.source: Check A2 (+2 6 8 1.333 false; +4 8 10 1.250 false; x2 8 12 1.500 true). The stage prints ratios with up to 2 decimals (1.33, 1.25, 1.5). The reveal quotes the first adding chip the learner pressed, recorded when the 'added-off' milestone fires.
claims.note: Arithmetic: 6 x 8 ratio 1.33, 8 x 10 ratio 1.25, 8 x 12 ratio 1.5; onRay matches; r2() prints 1.33, 1.25 and 1.5. artifacts/fact-check-wave-j/wj-econ-phys-math-geo/math.mjs.

claims.text: Two rectangles anchored at the same bottom-left corner have the same shape exactly when their side ratios are equal; then their top-right corners lie on one line through that corner.
claims.source: Similar triangles: the corner (w, h) lies on the line y = (6/4)x through the anchor exactly when h ÷ w = 1.5.
claims.note: Derivation: with the anchor at the origin, (w, h) lies on y = 1.5x exactly when h/w = 1.5 (same orientation, short side across).

claims.text: A shape is kept by multiplying every side by the same number; adding the same amount grows the short side by a bigger share than the long side.
claims.source: Adding d to sides a < b raises them by the fractions d/a and d/b, and d/a > d/b (here 2/4 = 50% against 2/6 = 33%).
claims.note: Derivation: adding d to sides a < b raises them by d/a > d/b. Recall: 10 x 15 scaled by 0.4 gives 4 x 6; subtracting 6 gives 4 x 9, a different ratio. Checks out.

recall.question: A 10 by 15 poster is shrunk so its short side is 4, without distorting it. What is its long side?
recall.why: Keeping the shape means multiplying both sides by the same number: 4 ÷ 10 = 0.4, and 15 × 0.4 = 6. Subtracting 6 from each side would give 4 by 9, a different shape.
